items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: We ran up on the highway to Erskine Hawkins' band truck. We pulled up to see what the trouble was, and he said they had left them there to guard the instruments.

ctx.x: So now, the military, they took many a car away from us. They had priority. And they'd put us off in a little one horse town, milk trains ran through and they would pass us by. And we'd be sitting on these big -- I guess you've seen them years ago, they had a -- looked like a wagon where they'd carry your baggage on. Flat, with wheels, and a tub. We'd try to sleep on them, waiting on a train and an express would come through there and throw cinders everywhere. And, boy, you talk about dirty. On top of our…

Now, we get to -- where was this -- I'm trying to think of this town where we had such a hangup. It was in Macon, Georgia. Macon, Georgia. We were using cars at this point. And we ran up on the highway to Erskine Hawkins' band truck. We pulled up to see what the trouble was, and he said they had

left them there to guard the instruments. So we drove on in to Macon. And while we were in Macon, the band truck driver fell asleep at the wheel, you know, behind the wheel. But he was off the highway, on the soft shoulder. So dark fell upon him. He was still asleep in the truck. So a flashlight shines down on him. He says, "Nigger, get that goddamn flashlight out of my face. Don't you see I'm asleep? You can wake a man up better than that." The door opened, they pulled him out, say, "Nigger, we've been watching…
